## Overview

You have (or will download) **one daily sea surface temperature field** on a regular lat–lon grid. You want **|∇SST|** — how sharply SST changes **across space** on that day — in units of **°C km⁻¹**. That is a common way to describe **thermal fronts** when linking oceanography to animal tracks.

This vignette does **not** download Copernicus files or fit movement models. It builds a **fine-resolution toy SST map**, computes the gradient the same way many reanalysis workflows do, and plots SST next to |∇SST| so you can see the front line up.

**You will need:** R, the [`terra`](https://rspatial.org/terra/) package, and a few minutes.

**This is not:** SST changing **over time** at one location; a “front probability” product; or a gradient of **regional mean** SST.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 1. Load terra




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# terra handles SpatRasters, sliding windows (focal), and quick maps.
pacman::p_load(terra)
```
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 2. Make a fine-grid toy SST field (°C)

Real products such as GLORYS12 often sit near **~0.08°** cell size. Here we use a **50 × 50** grid over **0.5° × 0.5°** of ocean (~**0.01°** per cell) so a **thermal front** shows as a narrow band instead of one fat block.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
n <- 50L # rows and columns — more cells = smaller cell size for a fixed map extent

# rast() allocates an empty grid: size, geographic bounds, and CRS (WGS84 lon/lat).
sst <- terra::rast(
  ncols = n,
  nrows = n,
  xmin = 170,
  xmax = 170.5,
  ymin = -45,
  ymax = -44.5,
  crs = "EPSG:4326"
)

# Fill SST in R: row = south→north, col = west→east (see ?terra::values).
sst_mat <- outer(1:n, 1:n, function(row, col) {
  # Smooth step in longitude: cold pool west, warm pool east — a simple front.
  front <- 1.5 * plogis((col - (n / 2 + 0.5)) * 0.15)
  # Slight lat trend so the field is not perfectly zonal everywhere.
  lat_trend <- 0.004 * row
  20 + front + lat_trend
})

# Push the matrix into the raster (row-major order).
terra::values(sst) <- matrix(sst_mat, nrow = n, ncol = n, byrow = TRUE)

# Check resolution in degrees before converting to km.
c(
  res_lon_deg = terra::res(sst)[1],
  res_lat_deg = terra::res(sst)[2],
  n_cells = terra::ncell(sst)
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
res_lon_deg res_lat_deg     n_cells 
       0.01        0.01     2500.00 
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(sst, main = "Toy SST (°C) — west/east front, fine cells")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/plot-sst-1.png){width=960}
:::
:::


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3. Cell width in kilometres

Finite differences give **°C per cell** until you divide by **km per cell**. Longitude spacing must be scaled by **cos(latitude)**.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# res() — cell size in map units (degrees here).
res <- terra::res(sst)

# Representative latitude for this small patch (OK for ~0.5° maps).
clat <- mean(
  terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# East–west km per cell decreases toward the poles.
dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
# North–south km per cell ≈ constant over a small area.
dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32

c(dx_km = dx_km, dy_km = dy_km, mean_lat = clat)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
      dx_km       dy_km    mean_lat 
  0.7905784   1.1132000 -44.7500000 
```


:::
:::


When you move to a real NetCDF, run `summary(SST)` — values should look like ocean **°C** (roughly 0–35), not Kelvin (~273+).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Centred differences and |∇SST|

We estimate ∂SST/∂x and ∂SST/∂y with **3×3 centred stencils** (`terra::focal`), then take the magnitude √(g_x² + g_y²).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sst_grad_magnitude_layer <- function(sst) {
  if (is.null(sst) || !terra::ncell(sst)) return(NULL)

  res <- terra::res(sst)
  clat <- mean(
    terra::yFromCell(sst, seq_len(min(5000L, terra::ncell(sst)))),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  dx_km <- as.numeric(res[1]) * 111.32 * cos(clat * pi / 180)
  dy_km <- as.numeric(res[2]) * 111.32
  if (!is.finite(dx_km) || dx_km <= 0 || !is.finite(dy_km) || dy_km <= 0) return(NULL)

  # Weights sum to zero on the centre row: (T_west + T_east) with ±0.5 → centred difference.
  w_x <- matrix(c(0, 0, 0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)
  w_y <- matrix(c(0, -0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5, 0), nrow = 3, ncol = 3)

  # focal slides the window; pad = TRUE keeps grid size (edge cells are less trustworthy).
  gx <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_x, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dx_km
  gy <- terra::focal(sst, w = w_y, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE, pad = TRUE) / dy_km

  sqrt(gx^2 + gy^2)
}

grad <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)
summary(grad, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   focal_sum       
 Min.   : 0.00871  
 1st Qu.: 0.01832  
 Median : 0.04062  
 Mean   : 0.92668  
 3rd Qu.: 0.06364  
 Max.   :16.80017  
```


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(sst, main = "SST (°C)")
plot(grad, main = expression("|"*nabla*SST|" (°C km"^-1*")"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/plot-both-1.png){width=960}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
:::


The **stripe of high |∇SST|** should sit where the west–east SST transition is — that is the front on this toy field.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Quick checks on the toy data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
flat <- sst * 0 + 20 # every cell the same temperature

g_flat <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(flat)
g_front <- sst_grad_magnitude_layer(sst)

mean_flat <- terra::global(g_flat, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
mean_front <- terra::global(g_front, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]

stopifnot(is.finite(mean_flat), is.finite(mean_front))
stopifnot(mean_front > mean_flat, mean_front > 0)

c(flat_mean = mean_flat, front_mean = mean_front)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 flat_mean front_mean 
 0.8554947  0.9266778 
```


:::
:::


If the front case does not beat the flat case, fix the stencil or units before using real SST.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Common mix-ups

| Idea | Reality |
|------|---------|
| “Gradient = day-to-day SST at a point” | That is a **time** derivative; here we difference **neighbour cells** on **one** day |
| “Kelvin breaks the math” | **Differences** in K equal differences in °C; still be consistent when you report SST |
| “Any high \|∇SST\| near land is an offshore front” | Coastal geometry often dominates near shore |
| “Fine grid captures every filament” | Even ~0.08° only **partly** resolves mesoscale fronts |

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Using this on real data

1. Open **one daily SST layer** (same grid you trust for point SST).  
2. Run the same function on that layer (or on each day in a loop).  
3. **`terra::extract`** |∇SST| at track longitudes/latitudes (watch lon convention: −180…180 vs 0…360).  
4. Aggregate to your analysis step (e.g. daily mean alongside other covariates).

Downloading GLORYS or other CMEMS products is its own workflow — see [Copernicus Marine](https://data.marine.copernicus.eu/) documentation.
